newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude closes 21 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude closes 21 cents higher.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures closed 21 cents higher Thursday as crude took the lead after a lacklustre performance by gasoil, brokers said.

IPE November Brent ended at $24.15 a barrel having reversed much of Wednedsay's losses. A floor dealer said Brent was on its way to testing resistance near the $24.50 a barrel level when it was sold off in the last few minutes of trade.
"Selling on December virtually in the last minute was quite aggressive. It went up following WTI where te locals got it through $25 a barrel but they sold it at the close too.
Nov WTI closed up 21 cents at $25.38 a barrel.
Earlier, IPE gasoil futures closed slightly higher and dealers said the rally in gas oil was more to keep up with Brent crude than with U.S. heating oil.
IPE Nov gas oil closed 25 cents up at $222.75 a tonne after dipping to a low of $222 a tonne earlier on Thursday.
"There was some liquidation and some stops were triggered on the upside. Gas oil mirrored what heating oil was doing and Brent had an effect," a futures broker said.
"It rallied back and it wasn't going to go down. It is now supported by Brent much more than it has been," he said, adding gasoil was suffering from weak demand in Europe.

"The cash market has gone a little bit off. We are now starting to see prices having a long-term effect on consumers and people are worried about it," the broker said. "Short term, there is no demand in the market. There is contractual demand, but short term, no."
Dec Brent failed to pierce through its intra-day high of $24.35 a barrel after touching a low of $23.72 in early trade.
Crude recovered in the afternoon session on a combination of political instability in Russia and U.S. data showing a fall in crude and distillate stocks last week.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin Thursday sacked his security chief, Alexander Lebeb.
Russia is the world's third largest oil producer and a key supplier of crude to European markets.
U.S. Department of Energy's latest weekly report confirmed the tight picture on heating oil markets as winter approaches, dealers said.
The DOE figures showed distillate stocks fell 900,000 barrels last week. Crude stocks were down 3.3 million barrels.
